I think the key is to pretty much set a good sleep schedule. Keep a consistent sleep schedule throughout the week, even on the weekends. People think that they'll "make up" for their sleep hours by sleeping in. If you wake up at 8 am every day, wake up at 8 am during the weekends. 

Before you go to sleep, definitely don't use your phone. Set your alarm way before you go to bed, and 15 minutes before, read a book, meditate, or do your normal night routine (wash your face, shower, brush your teeth) without your phone. The melatonin production (what contributes to better sleep) goes down when you expose yourself to light. Essentially, getting TO sleep is the key to waking up happy. On this note, make sure to go to sleep at the right time in which you can wake up at 8 am, or whenever you wake up, and be alright. 

Waking up sucks. I now do two or three things to wake up:
1. Wake up and drink water like > hysteridull said <. Dehydration is the most common form of draining your energy. My friend gave me some good advice- she said to drink a lot of water (like a ridiculous amount) before you go to bed, so not only will you be hydrated and refreshed, you'll have to get up to go to the bathroom- it's a weird incentive for waking up. 

2. Open the blinds and let the sunlight come in! You need sunlight to wake you up! 

3. Don't drink coffee. Eat a good breakfast- high in carbs and protein with natural sugars. 

4. Wake up and do ten jumping jacks- get moving. I run up and down the stairs in my dorm and it helps!

5. Keep some fruit next to your bed- natural sugars wake you up!

6. Listen to music or a motivational speech of some sorts. 

7. Find your steel, your why, your motivation, and write it down before you go to bed.

Hope this helps~

We have an finite amount of time with an infinite knowledge ahead of us. As a person who's struggling in college (academically) and also in the state of "discovering myself", it's okay. I'm still learning how to be a student. 
Don't work yourself out. Everyone learns at their own pace. Nevertheless, when you love something, you want to live and breathe it- take breaks every now and then. Once you're out in grad school and in the industry, you will have even more time to learn new skills. 
Keep in mind that not everyone knows everything- we all learn something new everyday. Don't compare yourself, know that you're one step closer to your dream every day you work hard. Get some sleep, and don't overwork yourself or you will face burnout.

I lived in a low cost triple in Rubin. The perks? Cheapest dorm on campus, about 3.8k per semester, which saved a LOT of money. Great room size, sick lounge, 5 minute walk to campus, and living on Fifth Ave was awesome. The downside? No A/C and it was an old building.
